primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{trench}': 'Net effectiveness of the offensive line and running back in controlling the line of scrimmage (yards, yd)', '\\Delta P_{pass}': 'Change in probability of facing a passing situation due to defensive adjustments'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that run-blocking efficiency directly translates to reduced pass-rush burden, with linear scaling between RYOE and pass-protection risk.

layer2.telemetry: Adjusted line yards and pass-rush win rate data

reasoning_traces.think:
The matchup analysis centers on the quarterback's ability to release the ball before the defensive front collapses the pocket. The offensive line's protection window is quantified by the NGS time-to-throw (2.80s), which serves as a ceiling for safe passing. Meanwhile, the running back's burst efficiency (RYOE = 0.0 yd) represents the counter-force against rushing pressure. When the defensive front is fully active (A_{front}=1), any reduction in offensive line performance or increase in blitz frequency reduces the net trench counter (C_{trench}). This creates a dual constraint: the quarterback must either throw faster or face higher interception risk. The breaking condition highlights the sensitivity to injury substitutions or tactical shifts, which can rapidly alter the equilibrium. These primitives form a closed-loop system where run-pass balance directly impacts pocket security, informing both GSI's predictive models and GSE's real-time decision trees.
